text: Which of the following increases the stability of a body?
options: Increasing the area of its base
Reducing the area of its base
explanation: A larger base area means the body can be tilted further before the line of action of its weight falls outside the base, so stability increases.

text: Which of the following statements about centre of gravity and stability is correct? I. The centre of gravity of a body depends on its temperature II. Stability is not affected by the position of the centre of gravity III. Lowering the centre of gravity increases the stability of a body
explanation:
Lowering the centre of gravity increases the stability of a body — this is correct.

The other two statements are not true: "Stability is not affected by the position of the centre of gravity" and "The centre of gravity of a body depends on its temperature" both misstate the physics.

So only III is correct.

text: Which of the following statements about centre of gravity and stability are correct? I. A body is in unstable equilibrium if it moves further away after a slight displacement II. Lowering the centre of gravity increases the stability of a body III. A narrow base makes a body more stable
explanation:
I and II are correct statements.

"A narrow base makes a body more stable" is false, so III must be excluded.

The answer is I and II only.

text: Which of the following statements about centre of gravity and stability are correct? I. Raising the centre of gravity increases stability II. text: Why are racing cars designed to be low and wide?
options: To lower the centre of gravity and widen the base, increasing stability
To reduce the mass of the car
To raise the centre of gravity and reduce weight
To increase friction with the air
explanation: A low centre of gravity and a wide base both increase stability by making it harder for the line of action of the weight to fall outside the base.

text: A uniform metre rule is balanced at its centre. A mass of 32g is placed 14cm from the pivot. How far from the pivot on the other side must a mass of 28g be placed to restore balance?

\(448 = 28d\)

\(d = 16\)cm
